If you conclude the right home for this check is inside that existing script, **stop and report** rather than editing it — that is a serialisation question, not an implementation choice.

## Zone 1 — Ruling and constraints (binding)

Filed by triage as part of the maintainer's 2026-08-25 family ruling (decision 甲/A1 on #6172, verbatim 「同意」): **every exported schema name has exactly one authority**, and a gate keeps that true after the cleanup lands so the #6172 / #6155 / #6169 / #6170 class cannot silently regrow.

The card's constraints are binding and each has a measurement behind it:

- **The matcher must discriminate.** Near-spellings and derived names are ⛔ **not** collisions.
- **Deliberate re-exports are not collisions** — `export { X } from './x'` is one declaration with many export sites. A **second declaration**, or an aliasing re-export that publishes an already-declared name, **is**.
- **The population refuses to collapse** — assert a minimum scanned-file count. A scan that finds nothing reads exactly like a scan that found nothing wrong.
- **Baseline discipline**: landing with an explicit, named baseline of today's known collisions is acceptable and it must **shrink** as #6172 / #6169 / #6170 land. ⛔ Silently exempting them forever is not.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism readings

⭐ **The house pattern you are asked to follow is not hypothetical — it was used again an hour ago and it caught two defects in itself.** PR #6195 is the precedent the card names; **PR #6337** (card #6186, merging now) is the fresher and more instructive instance. Read it before writing your matcher. What it establishes:

- **Two masks, not one.** A member access and a destructuring are code, so scan with comments *and* string literals blanked. But a computed access spells its key **as a string literal**, so blanking literals erases the very thing you are looking for. That leg must read comment-masked source where literals survive — and then require the **bracket itself** to be code, or the gate reds on quoted examples (including its own fixture table).
- ⚠️ **Its computed-access leg silently never fired** on the first authoring pass. The positive control is what caught it. A leg that cannot fire is the vacuous-green shape these gates exist to prevent, reproduced inside the gate.
- ⚠️ **It reddened on its own source** the moment it was committed — the moment a tracked-files population first contained it. Expect the same: your gate will name schema types in its fixtures and its diagnostic. Solve it with a real discriminator, ⛔ not a filename exemption.
- **Negative controls are the load-bearing half.** Every one should be a spelling **this repository really writes**, cited where it lives. An assertion that reds on legitimate code gets deleted by the first person who hits it, and the claim goes back to unguarded — worse than never writing it.

⚠️ **Re-measure the known collisions yourself.** The card cites #6172 (`FormField`, `MarkdownSchema`, `KanbanSchema`) and #6155 (`KanbanCard` ×4), but those family cards are landing right now — several merged today. Your baseline must be **today's** measurement, not the card's. If a cited collision is already cleaned, say so; if your scan finds collisions the family cards never named, that is new information and it belongs in the report.

## Zone 3 — Suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

A root-suite test under `scripts/__tests__/` looks right to me — it inherits the vitest run that already exists, needs no workflow wiring, and #6337 just demonstrated the whole shape end to end. ⛔ My guess, not a constraint: if a `check:` script is the better home by this repo's conventions, take it and say why (and note that a `check:` script needs its own workflow trigger wiring, including its own path in that workflow's `paths:` filter — see #6321).

## Gates

Derive from your diff. A new gate owes a test that proves it discriminates, shown red-before / green-after in the report. Follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s own verdict on whether a changeset is owed; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label (#4912). Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe and quote each gate's own verdict line.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** with your branch — ⚠️ under `mode:subagent` your session ID is identical to mine (objectstack#12220), so the **branch** is what distinguishes your claim. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read it back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #6273`.

## ACCEPT — PR #6348

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Read against the diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report.

### ⭐ The number the card did not know: 46 collisions, and 42 of them have no owner

The card's baseline clause says a ratchet naming today's population is acceptable, *"silently exempting them forever is not."* The measured population is **46 names**, of which the family cards (#6172 / #6155 / #6169 / #6170) name **four**. So the ratchet can drain to 42 as those land and then **stops** — which is the shape the card's own clause warns about, reached honestly rather than by exemption.

That is why filing **#6349** (the full site table, now labelled `finding`) is the load-bearing half of this delivery. ⚠️ Triage should read the ratchet baseline as *"42 names awaiting an owner"*, not as *"cleanup in progress"*.

### The card's citations were stale, and the re-measurement is what proves the population is the right one

I re-derived all of it on `origin/main` rather than accepting the report:

| the card says | measured | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `FormField` collides (#6172) | **1** declaration, `packages/types/src/form.ts:911` | ⛔ **already clean** — the cited list is stale by one |
| `KanbanCard` ×4 (#6155) | exactly **4** files | ✅ matches #6155's own count |
| `MarkdownSchema`, `KanbanSchema` | still live | ✅ |

⭐ The `KanbanCard` agreement is the important one and the report names why: it is the evidence that this gate's population is **co-extensive** with the one the family cards counted by hand. A new scanner that agreed with nothing would be measuring something else and nobody could tell.

Two of the folded-in findings I checked personally because they are the most consequential — both hold:

- **`ActionSchema`** — `packages/types/src/crud.ts:67` **and** `ui-action.ts:374`, both inside `packages/types`
- **`BreadcrumbItem`** — `data-display.ts:1225` **and** `navigation.ts:179`, likewise

⚠️ Those two are worse than a cross-package duplicate: a consumer importing from the barrel **cannot say which one it meant**, and no error tells them. Also folded in: `KanbanColumn` collides across the **exact same four files** as `KanbanCard`, and no card mentions it — whoever takes #6155 is already standing in front of the second half.

### The gate's own discipline

**Root-suite test over a `check:` script**, with the reason given rather than the preference: it inherits the existing vitest run and needs no workflow job or `paths:` entry — which, per #6321, is a whole class of defect avoided rather than a convenience. #6337 is cited as the house precedent for the shape, which is what my order asked.

⭐ **Reverse verification at tree level, on the real population** — and the report says exactly why fixtures alone would not do: *"fixture positive controls alone would only prove the analyzer fires."* So it injected a genuine second `export interface MarkdownRendererProps` into a real package and watched the gate name it with both sites. Mutation confirmed by **anchored grep AND blob hash as hard gates that abort the run and void the readings** — not by an editor's exit code. Restore via `git checkout HEAD --` with an absolute path (never the bare form, which restores from a polluted index), proven three ways: blob back to `e71cadc154…`, marker count 0, `git diff HEAD` empty.

**Discrimination**: deliberate re-exports (`export { X } from './x'`, `export *`, `X as X`) are one declaration with many export sites and are not counted; near-spellings anchored out at both ends. **No build leg exists to invalidate** — the gate reads tracked source through vitest, nothing resolves through a `dist` — stated rather than skipped.

### On #5899 — the constraint was met, and better than met

⛔ `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` untouched, as ordered. But the dev did more than avoid the file: it established that **no serialisation question arose**, because that gate answers *"a local declaration sharing a name with an `@objectstack/spec` export must be derived from the spec"* — a different population and a different verdict from *"two authorities inside objectui"*. That is the difference between obeying a boundary and understanding it.

### Gates

All green at `78a9140c9`, each quoted from its own verdict line. Notably `type-check:scripts` was proven **not** to be a not-measured green: `tsc --listFiles` reports 1 hit for the new file, so it really is in the program. `check-changeset-presence` says none is owed and none was added. Narrowing declared: repo-wide `pnpm lint` not run locally, `lint:root` covers the root-level tree this one-file diff lives in, CI runs the full farm regardless.

**Channel note recorded, not worked around**: direct REST to `api.github.com` is refused for this seat, so a byte-level diff of the stored card body against an independent fetch was impossible; the no-truncation verdict rests on the API-delivered body being structurally complete, and the report says so instead of claiming a check it could not run.
